summary:
The BAA ties AtliQ’s services to HIPAA obligations and references the yet‑unsigned MSA. Key risks already flagged include offshore PHI handling, uncapped liability, $5 M cyber‑insurance demand, and subcontractor bans. An additional concern is the vague safeguard language that could expose AtliQ to liability for alleged insufficient HIPAA protection.

Harrington Health Systems Inc · BAA · AtliQ Inc as supplier. 18 finding(s): 4 critical, 7 high, 6 medium, 1 low; 1 potential conflict(s) with past commitments; 1 check(s) could not be verified.

findings.title: BAA bars any non-US subcontractor — including AtliQ's Pune team
findings.explanation: Potential conflict with how AtliQ delivers. §4.2 requires every approved subcontractor to be a US-organised entity with US-located personnel, and §1.5 defines Subcontractor to include Business Associate's Affiliates. AtliQ Inc sub-contracts delivery to AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd in Pune; that model would not be allowed at all — not even for de-identified data, which the CareBridge BAA permitted. Staffing, price and timeline need to be re-planned around US-only personnel, or the clause negotiated.
findings.contract_quote: Each approved Subcontractor shall be organized under the laws of a State of the United States, and all of its personnel performing Services shall be located in the United States.

evidence.quote: Delivery teams for both entities sit in Pune; AtliQ Inc sub-contracts delivery to AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd under an intercompany agreement.

findings.title: No subcontractor BAA for anyone who would touch this client's PHI
findings.explanation: HIPAA flow-down requires every subcontractor — including AtliQ's own Pune entity and any freelancer — to sign a subcontractor BAA with matching terms before access. The only one AtliQ has (intercompany, Oct 2025) is engagement-specific: it covers the CareBridge engagement only, de-identified data only, and ends with the CareBridge BAA on 5 Oct 2026. It does not cover this client, despite the 27 Sep assumption that it 'should do'. The freelancer brought in for this client (Kriti Data Labs, C-037; Daniel Ortiz, C-047) has a contractor agreement and NDA in draft but no subcontractor BAA.

findings.title: Uncapped liability for AtliQ under §8.2
findings.explanation: AtliQ's exposure under the cited provisions — including its indemnity obligations — is carved out of any cap. The carve-out covers data-security / privacy events, where regulatory fines, notification and credit-monitoring costs are the largest exposure. AtliQ's position has been liability capped at 1x fees; Karandeep walked away from Kessler Mobility (~€120k) over 'liable without limitation'.

findings.title: Full liability for subcontractor acts
findings.explanation: Clause 4.4 makes AtliQ liable for any act or omission of its subcontractors as if they were its own, potentially expanding exposure beyond any fee‑based liability caps elsewhere in the BAA. Verify if AtliQ can obtain subcontractor indemnities or limit this responsibility.
findings.contract_quote: Business Associate shall remain fully responsible for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors as if they were Business Associate's own.

findings.title: Requires $5M cyber cover — AtliQ holds $1M
findings.explanation: The contract requires cyber liability insurance of $5,000,000. AtliQ's cyber policy is $1M (Karandeep, tracker C-046 / Harrington huddle 27 Sep). Signing would put AtliQ in breach from day one unless cover is increased or the requirement negotiated. The gap has not yet been raised with the client (meeting note 27 Sep).
findings.contract_quote: Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S.
escalation_hints: Check with Finance / insurance broker — current cover vs requirement.

findings.contract_quote: Business Associate shall not use PHI, or any data derived from PHI, to train, tune or evaluate any machine learning or artificial intelligence model other than models developed exclusively for Covered Entity under the Master Services Agreement.

findings.title: Termination for breach with undefined cure period
findings.explanation: The BAA lets the Covered Entity terminate immediately or after a cure period it defines, giving AtliQ little control over termination timing and potential abrupt loss of the contract.
findings.contract_quote: If Covered Entity determines that Business Associate has violated a material term of this BAA, Covered Entity may, at its option, (a) provide Business Associate an opportunity to cure within a period specified by Covered Entity, and terminate this BAA and the Master Services Agreement if Business Associate does not cure; or (b) immediately terminate this BAA and the Master Services Agreement if cure is not possible.

findings.contract_quote: Any ambiguity in this BAA shall be resolved to permit Covered Entity to comply with HIPAA. In the event of any conflict between this BAA and the Master Services Agreement with respect to PHI, this BAA shall control.

findings.title: Audit rights may impose operational burden
findings.explanation: The BAA allows the Covered Entity to audit Business Associate facilities with 48‑hour notice and requires prompt remediation of any deficiency, which could disrupt AtliQ's operations and incur remediation costs.
findings.contract_quote: Covered Entity or its designee may inspect and audit Business Associate's and any Subcontractor's facilities, systems, books, records, policies and procedures relating to PHI upon forty-eight (48) hours' notice, at any time during the term of this BAA and for so long as Business Associate retains any PHI. Business Associate shall promptly remediate any deficiency identified.

findings.title: 30‑day return or destruction requirement
findings.explanation: AtliQ must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days of termination, which may be impractical for large data sets and could lead to breach of contract if not met.
findings.contract_quote: Upon termination or expiration of the Master Services Agreement, Business Associate shall, within thirty (30) days, return or destroy all PHI, including PHI in the possession of Subcontractors, retain no copies, and certify destruction in writing. If return or destruction is infeasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to such PHI and limit further uses and disclosures to those purposes that make return or destruction infeasible.

findings.title: Undefined safeguard standards may create liability
findings.explanation: Section 3.1 obligates AtliQ to implement "administrative, physical and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect" e‑PHI, but provides no measurable standards. This ambiguity could lead to disputes or liability if the Covered Entity deems the safeguards inadequate, especially given the uncapped liability elsewhere. Clarify required frameworks (e.g., NIST 800‑53) or include a compliance audit provision.
findings.contract_quote: Business Associate shall implement administrative, physical and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic PHI, and shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164.
